In the figure above, $∠BOA$ is a straight angle, $\overset{\to }{OD}$ and $\overset{\to }{OE}$ are the bisectors of $∠AOC$ and $∠BOC$, respectively. If $m∠DOC=4x$ and $m∠COE=5x$, find the value of $x.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/77adc8fb9c00bd21579a8697f8b11c228e3864e657f2b991be4d09b4c6f5a96d.png)

Since $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠AOC$, we have 

$$
m∠AOD=m∠DOC=4x.
$$

Since $\overset{\to }{OE}$ is the bisector of $∠BOC$, we have 

$$
m∠EOB=m∠COE=5x.
$$

Now, by the angle addition postulate, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠AOD+m∠DOC+m∠EOB+m∠COE & ={180}^{∘} \\ 4x+4x+5x+5x & ={180}^{∘} \\ 18x & ={180}^{∘} \\ x & ={10}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/0e112d00ddcb34c30a490d1a71e3e0b4a2c698707e3890666ac4e299c3ca37cd.png)

In the figure above, $∠BOA$ is a straight angle,  and $\overset{\to }{OD}$ is the bisector of $∠COA.$ If $m∠BOD={107}^{∘},$ find $m∠BOC.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/2d75ac364d71d8dd6cf35cfe7f8966b603c3cbee0bc5adff5f7dadf7468bab4c.png)

Since the angles $∠DOA$ and $∠BOD$ are supplementary, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠DOA & ={180}^{∘}-m∠BOD \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{107}^{∘} \\  & ={73}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore,

$$
m∠DOA=m∠COD={73}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOC & =m∠BOD-m∠COD \\  & ={107}^{∘}-{73}^{∘} \\  & ={34}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/187b52aa0450e940bd644f9d1ae560a735c7e10e18157ecba910a6a817c11797.png)

In the figure above, $∠BOA$ is a straight angle,  and $\overset{\to }{OC}$ is the bisector of $∠BOD.$ If $m∠DOA={58}^{∘},$ find $m∠COA.$
questions.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14237394/assets/9d7c5789c579b9292beb17ad03ae6239083ffa70fe5ec581da33cd488e365344.png)

Since the angles $∠BOD$ and $∠DOA$ are supplementary, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠BOD & ={180}^{∘}-m∠DOA \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{58}^{∘} \\  & ={122}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

The bisector of an angle divides the angle into two congruent angles. Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COD & =\frac{m∠BOD}{2} \\  & =\frac{{122}^{∘}}{2} \\  & ={61}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠COA & =m∠COD+m∠DOA \\  & ={61}^{∘}+{58}^{∘} \\  & ={119}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
